To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the primary photodissocia- tion dynamics of allylchloride upon excitation at the vacuum ultraviolet wavelength of 193 nm are dominated by two channels: (1) C–Cl bond scission, and (2) HCl elimination.

the primary photodisscociation of ally chloride at 193 nm proceeds via four reaction channels: C-Cl bond fission producing unstable allyl radical, excited state C-Cl bond dissociation producing Cl atoms, HCl elimination with high translational excitation to the products, and HCl elimination with low translational energy to the products.

the primary dissociation of allylchloride at 193 nm proceeds through the following channels: C-Cl bond fission to form unstable allyl radicals and chlorine, excited state C-Cl bond cleavage to produce chlorine atoms and allyl, hydrogen chloride elimination to form hydrogen chloride and a mass 40 product (predominantly allyl), and hydrogen chloride elimination to produce hydrogen chloride and a high energy mass 40 product.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the photodissociative reactions of the allyl halide molecules, and in particular the dynamics of the primary and secondary reactions of the nascent products formed.
the photodissociative behavior of the C–Cl and C–H bonds of allyl chloride at 193 nm, and with the dynamics of subsequent secondary radical reactions.
the primary and secondary reaction dynamics of the photodissociative processes occurring in the photodissocation of allyl chloride at 193 nm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the primary photodisscociation dynamics of 193 nm allyl chloride is a complex mixture of four primary reaction channels with the C–Cl bond breaking to produce allyl radicals as the dominant channel.
193 nm photolysis of allyl chloride produces Cl atoms and HCl in a variety of kinetic energy distributions, and the nascent products undergo a variety of secondary reactions.

the 193 nm photochemistry of allyl chloride produces Cl atoms and HCl molecules, with the former being produced by both excited state and ground state bond fission and the latter by HCl elimination from both allyl chloride and the nascent allyl radical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the C–Cl bond is the primary bond that dissociates in the 193-nm photodissociations of allyl chloride, and that this bond fission occurs in two different electronic states, with the excited state C–HCl bond fission pathway being the dominant reaction channel.
we have shown that the primary photofragmentation dynamics are dominated by the fast C–Cl bond cleavage and the slow C–Cl bond breaking.

the 193 nm dissociation of allylchloride produces a mixture of Cl atoms and HCl molecules, and that the Cl atom products are produced by both direct dissociation of the excited allylchloride molecule and by dissociation of the unstable allyl radicals produced by the C–Cl bond cleavage channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a large percentage of the nascent allyl radicals formed in the primary reaction channels undergo secondary radical reactions, producing a large percentage of H atoms in the system.
there is no evidence for the formation of allyl radical products from the 193 nm photoexcitation of allyl chloride.
the C–Cl bond dissociation energy in allyl chloride is not 3.7 eV as measured previously by photoionization mass spectroscopy but 3.9 eV, which is in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
